name: squash-domesticated-guila-naquitz
description: Foragers in a Mexican cave began growing squash, among the first domesticated crops of the Americas.

name: cacao-use-santa-ana-la-florida
description: People of the upper Amazon were the first known users of cacao, the plant that gives us chocolate.

name: zapotecs-found-monte-alban
description: Zapotec leaders levelled a mountaintop in Oaxaca and raised a hilltop capital of plazas, temples and tombs.

name: el-mirador-maya-city-rises
friendly_name: El Mirador Rises as a Maya City
description: In the jungles of Guatemala, a Maya city raised huge pyramids, among them La Danta, one of the largest ever built.

name: teotihuacan-city-founded
description: A planned city with broad avenues began to grow in the Valley of Mexico, later the largest in the Americas.

name: chiapa-de-corzo-long-count-stela
description: A carved stela in southern Mexico bore the oldest surviving date in the Maya calendar's Long Count system.

name: lord-of-sipan-burial
friendly_name: Lord of Sipan Buried in Gold
description: A Moche ruler was laid to rest in Peru with gold, turquoise and sacrificed attendants, a tomb found intact.

name: teotihuacan-conquers-tikal
description: Warriors linked to a great Mexican city arrived at a Maya capital in Guatemala, and its king died the same day.

name: copan-dynasty-founded
description: K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' founded the royal line of a Maya city in Honduras that ruled for four centuries.

name: teotihuacan-burned-collapse
description: Fire swept the ceremonial heart of the great Mexican city, whose population then dwindled away.

name: calakmul-defeats-tikal
description: The Snake kingdom's alliance overthrew Tikal, the leading Maya city, and dominated the lowlands for generations.

name: pakal-tomb-sealed-palenque
description: The great Maya ruler of Palenque was buried in a stone sarcophagus deep inside the Temple of the Inscriptions.

name: tikal-temple-i-built
description: A steep funerary pyramid rose over the tomb of a Maya king in Guatemala, facing the city's Great Plaza.

name: chan-chan-rises
friendly_name: Chan Chan Rises in Coastal Peru
description: The Chimu built a vast adobe capital on the Peruvian coast, with walled palaces and carved friezes.

name: chichen-itza-rises
description: A Maya city in Yucatan grew into a major centre, later known for its stepped pyramid El Castillo.

name: cusco-founded-legend
description: By tradition, Manco Capac led his people to the Andean valley where the Inca capital was raised.

name: pachacuti-becomes-inca
description: After defeating invaders, a new Inca ruler began turning a highland kingdom into a vast empire.

name: inca-conquer-chimu
description: Inca armies took the Chimu realm on the Peruvian coast, its richest rival and the builders of Chan Chan.

name: tenochtitlan-conquers-tlatelolco
description: The Aztec capital defeated its twin island city and took over its busy market and trade networks.

name: templo-mayor-dedicated
description: The Aztec twin-shrined temple pyramid was rededicated with ceremonies said to include thousands of sacrifices.

name: moctezuma-ii-crowned
description: The ninth Aztec tlatoani took the throne of an empire at its height; the Spaniards later held him captive.
